terminology.details: Checkpoint and fingerprint are defined in the target. The linked prerequisites let me explain SFT as supervised continuation using correct answer demonstrations, IGNORE as excluding direct answer loss while retaining question input, logits as candidate scores, EOS as the segment-ending token, and byte-token positions as different from printed Chinese characters. Dense uses one feed-forward rule set per layer; the product MoE routes to multiple experts. For DPO, policy is the currently updated model and reference is the fixed starting comparison model. Joint's text/image/audio description supplies the intended meaning of modality here. No unresolved term blocks the argument.

examples.details: The row is the first style task, with question 照抄數字29，只要答案。 and demonstration DIRECT:29. The nine ASCII answer bytes plus EOS give ten SFT targets; the full-text version reports 43. The table's 300/1400/600/100 are completed parameter updates, and 0/42/75/71 are whole-task successes out of the same 84 validation questions. The 42 SFT successes are all 42 text tasks, rather than half success in every skill. Joint keeps all 42 text tasks and adds 33 of 42 modality tasks, leaving nine failures. The later DPO score drops by four, so newest is not automatically best. The 364409/647067/249100 target counts count repeated supervised byte/EOS positions, not unique articles; DPO's 41403 includes only rehearsal cross-entropy positions, so it is not a like-for-like total computation budget. These are explanations of the prose's cited earlier experiment, not measurements I reran.

program_explanation.details: I can track every important line. The seed fixes the random setup; build_dataset returns splits and an unused manifest; next selects one style row and print exposes it. default_config(dense=True) builds a random Dense model. The loop switches only the pretrain flag; prepare_batch returns input fields and next-position labels. model(**batch) unpacks input fields as named arguments; result[logits] provides candidate scores; masked_loss counts non-IGNORE labels. (labels != IGNORE).sum() counts effective targets, and loss.isfinite() checks for an ordinary finite number. There is no backward call, optimizer, or parameter update. I saved predictions before running the exact fence in a bounded CPU process. It printed the stated row, 43 pretraining targets, 10 SFT targets, and finite=True for both. Finite loss establishes that this short data/scoring path connects, not that training worked or that one target scheme is better.

I ran only the small exercise, not the main training stages.
